raw_case_text: A 37-year-old male from Georgia came to France in October 2012. He had HIV infection since 2006 inconstantly treated with HAART. Other medical conditions were adrenal insufficiency, cirrhosis due to chronic HCV, and treatment-controlled tuberculosis. VL was diagnosed in 2010 and treated in Georgia with meglumine antimoniate and L-AmB (doses and schedules unknown). In November 2012, he presented hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathies, infiltrated cutaneous lesions, anemia, number of CD4 lymphocytes = 133/mm3, viral load < 50 copies/mL, and parasitemia of 6 Leishmania/ml. He received a course of L-AmB followed by maintenance therapy for 5 months (Fig 1B). In May 2013, he had weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, anemia, number of CD4 lymphocytes = 177/mm3, viral load < 40 copies/mL and parasitemia of 12 Leishmania/ml. L-AmB treatment was intensified, but renal insufficiency and acute thrombocytopenia occurred. In June, the splenomegaly and parasitemia remained unchanged. A course of meglumine antimoniate was administered. Despite pre-existing liver disorders, the treatment was well tolerated except for mild neutropenia. One month later, a marked clinical improvement was observed and parasitemia decreased to 0.2 Leishmania/ml. In July, maintenance treatment with miltefosine (150 mg/day for 3 months) was started. Parasitemia was negative, the number of CD4 lymphocytes increased from 169 to 540/mm3, and viral load was undetectable. Parasitemia remained negative through 18 months.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 37-year-old male presented with hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and infiltrated skin lesions.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 37-year-old male from Georgia presented in November 2012 with hepatosplenomegaly, generalized lymphadenopathies, infiltrated skin lesions, and anemia. He was treated with an induction course of L-AmB followed by 5 months of maintenance therapy. In May 2013, he suffered a relapse with progressive weight loss, persistent hepatosplenomegaly, and anemia. Intensification of L-AmB induced acute renal insufficiency and thrombocytopenia without splenic reduction. In June 2013, he was transitioned to meglumine antimoniate, followed by oral miltefosine maintenance, which achieved complete clinical remission and parasitemia clearance.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection diagnosed in 2006 (intermittently treated with HAART); adrenal insufficiency; liver cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection; treatment-controlled pulmonary tuberculosis. Prior visceral leishmaniasis diagnosed in Georgia in 2010, treated with meglumine antimoniate and L-AmB.
subjective.review_of_systems: Weight loss, anorexia, fatigue, infiltrated skin lesions. Denied fever during late relapse.

objective.physical_examination: Cachectic male with palpable hepatosplenomegaly, generalized peripheral lymphadenopathies, and diffuse infiltrated cutaneous lesions. Spleen size remained enlarged despite initial therapy.
objective.routine_investigations: Anemia on presentation. Following intensified L-AmB, developed acute renal insufficiency and acute thrombocytopenia. Transient mild neutropenia occurred during antimonial therapy. CD4+ T-cell count: 133/mm^3 in November 2012; 177/mm^3 in May 2013; increased from 169 to 540/mm^3 in July 2013. HIV viral load < 50 copies/mL initially and < 40 copies/mL in May 2013.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive Diagnosis: Relapsing visceral leishmaniasis with cutaneous involvement (PKDL/disseminated) in an HIV-coinfected patient with HCV cirrhosis and adrenal insufficiency.
Diagnostic Confirmation: Quantitative blood PCR demonstrated parasitemia of 6 Leishmania/mL in November 2012, rising to 12 Leishmania/mL during the May 2013 relapse, declining to 0.2 Leishmania/mL following antimonial therapy, and becoming undetectable on miltefosine.
Differentials Ruled Out: Progression of HCV cirrhosis, recurrence of tuberculosis, and lymphoproliferative malignancy.
Treatment & Clinical Course: Received L-AmB induction and 5 months maintenance. Relapse in May 2013 failed intensified L-AmB due to nephrotoxicity and thrombocytopenia. In June 2013, treated with a course of meglumine antimoniate, which was well tolerated despite cirrhosis (mild neutropenia only) and reduced parasitemia to 0.2 Leishmania/mL. Switched in July 2013 to maintenance oral miltefosine (150 mg/day for 3 months), resulting in complete clinical recovery, CD4+ count reconstitution to 540/mm^3, and sustained undetectable parasitemia through 18 months of follow-up.
